results.description: Innovation S5: evidence-request policies on SYNTHETIC JSON-only cases with a hidden latent truth. Replaces the circular 'next-best-evidence top-1 vs resolving document' headline.

design.extraction: oracle: truth.oracle_extraction through the real checks and contradiction builder, with the oracle page text scanned for embedded instructions (no OCR, no PDF)

held_out_family.chosen: 2026-10-14, before any simulation was run (the Phase 4 spec's example)
held_out_family.rule: cases containing it were never simulated during development (development-split cases with it are never simulated); test-split cases with it are reported only under held_out_family
held_out_family.disclosure: the engine's detection of this problem (open_items_insurance.claims_history_items) was written and unit-tested by the engine build on other generated packets (seed 4040) before the simulator existed; the hold-out covers simulator development and every simulation result

policies.voi: highest nonzero VOI first; stop when no open request has a VOI above zero (innovation S5 rule)
policies.voi_lookahead: voi, then the zero-VOI request with the highest nonzero lookahead value (an addition)
policies.checklist: every open request in the fixed severity order of evidence.open_items.PROBLEM_ORDER (the catalog has no severity field)
policies.random: every open request in a seeded shuffled order
policies.oracle: knows the truth: cheapest cost-weighted request sequence that reaches the full-information recommendation (exhaustive uniform-cost search over request orders; only cases with at most 4 open requests at the start)

design.headline_policy: voi (the specified S5 stopping rule); voi_lookahead is reported as an addition

priors_variants.latent_x0.5: prior of the latent (true) option x0.5, renormalized
priors_variants.latent_x1.5: prior of the latent (true) option x1.5, renormalized
priors_variants.latent_removed: latent (true) option removed from the option set, renormalized

metrics.requests_per_case: number of requests the policy made
metrics.cost_weighted_requests_per_case: sum of the catalog cost weights of those requests
metrics.zero_value_requests_per_case: requests whose VOI was 0 just before (under the variant's priors) and whose reveal did not change the recommendation
metrics.decision_error_rate: share of cases whose final recommendation differs from the full-information recommendation (every planted problem revealed)
metrics.requests_to_stable_when_reached: requests after which the recommendation equals the full-information recommendation and stays; cases ending on another recommendation are left out

reading_notes: The voi policy only makes requests whose VOI is above zero, so its zero-value request count is 0 by construction; the comparison is how many zero-value requests the other policies make.

Scaling the latent option's prior by 0.5 or 1.5 keeps every prior above zero, so it cannot change WHICH requests have a VOI above zero, only their values and order; for the voi policy, differences between the documented, x0.5 and x1.5 rows come only from the order of several nonzero requests. Removing the latent option can change which requests have value. voi_lookahead also depends on which option is most likely.
Checklist, random and oracle make the same requests under every priors variant; only the VOI they are valued at, and so the zero-value count, can change.

The full-information recommendation reveals every planted problem. A planted problem that no open item stands for cannot be requested by any policy; decision_error_rate_when_every_planted_problem_detected leaves those cases out.

requests_to_stable_when_reached averages only the cases where the run ends on the full-information recommendation, so its case set differs between policies; the paired comparison uses the cases both reached.

The oracle stops at the first state whose recommendation equals the full-information recommendation. That state need not be the full-information state: when a planted problem is undetected, another open problem can give the same recommendation, so 'oracle reached' does not mean every problem was revealed.

The full-information recommendation is what the SYNTHETIC reference policy (agent/policy.py) gives once every planted problem is revealed; it is the benchmark here, not a claim about the right lending or underwriting decision.

headline.group: test split without the held-out family, all lines, documented priors
headline.comparison: voi minus checklist, per case, paired bootstrap (1,000 resamples, seed 42)

not_claimable: real time or cost savings (cost weights and priors are planning assumptions)
that the VOI score is optimal or an economic model
extraction accuracy (the simulator uses the generator's oracle extraction)
anything about real applications: every case is SYNTHETIC

results.description: Evidence-to-Action Engine on SYNTHETIC document packets: claim statuses, benign vs unsupported explanations, next-best-evidence agreement (circular), top-request reveal, calculation agreement and decision stability, in oracle-extraction and pipeline-extraction modes. Simulated documents only; no real-world accuracy claim.

modes.oracle: engine on the generator's perfect extraction (truth.oracle_extraction) with the oracle page text scanned for embedded instructions (evidence.simulator_cases.prepare_case): isolates the engine
modes.pipeline: engine on the Phase 2 pipeline output of the packet PDF (rules extractor, Tesseract OCR for pages without a text layer): end to end

table.not_computable_rule: not computable on the truth's as-documented application -> UNKNOWN (conditional)

excluded_by_design.MODEL-: UNKNOWN by the honesty rule: no Phase 1 model is trained on these commercial packets
excluded_by_design.FEATURE-: model feature claims: only produced by a model estimator, none applies here
excluded_by_design.ASSUME-: ASSUMPTION by design: the clean screening assumption (KYC lists not used in this evaluation)

protocol.development_note: The expected claim-status table (src/uwcopilot/evidence/evaluation.py) and every metric definition were developed on the dev split (240 packets) and frozen before the first test-split run of this script. An earlier, interrupted attempt at this evaluation printed the test split's problem-type and resolving-request counts (truth composition only; the engine was not run on test packets) before the table was written.

versions.risk_model: not evaluated (no Phase 1 model applies to these SYNTHETIC commercial packets)

claim_status.note: Expected statuses come from the truth's planted problems and missing documents (evidence/evaluation.py, table version and sha256 below). Most claims are expected VERIFIED, so overall accuracy is dominated by them; open_expected is the accuracy on claims expected CONFLICTING or UNKNOWN. ABSENT: a claim the table requires is not in the ledger (also every required claim of a packet whose application did not validate). A packet whose application did not validate has no ledger, so its VERIFIED claims cannot be scored: read the accuracy together with 'evaluable'. The claim id scheme of the table and of the ledger were written by the same author, so this measures detection and propagation, not an independent claim taxonomy.

MODEL-.reason: UNKNOWN by the honesty rule: no Phase 1 model is trained on these commercial packets

FEATURE-.reason: model feature claims: only produced by a model estimator, none applies here

ASSUME-.reason: ASSUMPTION by design: the clean screening assumption (KYC lists not used in this evaluation)

benign_vs_unsupported.note: Restated with docintel's matching (evaluation_problems.py) on this mode's contradictions: one representative contradiction per detected benign or unsupported problem; 'unknown' counts as wrong. In pipeline mode this repeats the Phase 2 measurement.

next_best_evidence_agreement_circular.label: CIRCULAR: the generator's resolving_request and the engine's request rules were written by the same author, so agreement mainly shows that two hand-written tables match. It is not evidence that the ranking is useful; the innovation S5 simulator (section 'simulator') is the non-circular evaluation.
next_best_evidence_agreement_circular.definition: Per planted problem. Its items are the open items that stand for it (evidence.simulator_cases.matches). Eligible: one of its items belongs to a ranked request with VOI > 0. top_1 / top_3: the truth's resolving request (id, and every parameter the truth gives; a multi-document request agrees when it lists the truth's document) is ranked first / in the first three. mapping: among problems with an item, the request of one of its items agrees with the truth's, whatever the rank.

top_request_reveal.definition: Per packet with at least one ranked request: the rank-1 request is answered with the latent (true) resolution of the planted problems its items stand for (applied in the simulator's canonical order), the reference policy is re-run, and changed = the recommendation differs from the current one. Packets whose rank-1 request stands for no planted problem, and reveals whose levers could not be applied, are counted apart and are not in the denominator.

calculation_agreement.note: The reference policy's calculations on the engine's application against the same calculations on truth.application_as_documented. A calculation of a packet whose application did not validate counts as 'missing' (disagreement). In oracle mode this checks the document-to-application mapping.

tolerances.usd, usd_per_sqft: within $1.00 or 0.5% of the truth value, whichever is larger

scenarios_and_stability.note: Counts over evaluable packets. A family's first flip is the smallest tested shock that changes the reference recommendation ('none': every tested shock keeps it; 'untested': no scenario of the family could be evaluated, e.g. no verified revenue). Stability is a property of the reference policy on these SYNTHETIC cases.

paired_pipeline_minus_oracle.note: pipeline minus oracle on the same packets; paired packet-level bootstrap (1,000 resamples, seed 42)

not_claimable: real-world accuracy of the engine or of the extraction (SYNTHETIC packets written by the project author)
that the next-best-evidence ranking is useful because it agrees with the generator (the metric is circular)
that the value-of-information score is optimal or an economic model
anything about risk-model estimates: model PD and expected loss are UNKNOWN by design in this phase
